gaps.sentence: Can I ask you ___ questions about your trip?
gaps.hint: polite request with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'A few questions' means some questions and is the natural pattern in polite requests.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: The hotel was full, so we had to look for ___ hotel.
gaps.explanation: 'Another hotel' means some other, unspecified one; 'the other hotel' would imply exactly two known hotels.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ of the villagers had ever seen a passport.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly any of' = almost none of; 'hardly none' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
